- Overestimate prices when sentiment is low or neutral (especially after recent spikes), as market cooling often undercuts forecasts.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves when sentiment is positive or recently high — models overreact to optimism, then fail to adjust for reversal.
- Overshoot after strong upward moves (e.g., 70+ to 75+), then fail to correct — model inertia keeps prices high when sentiment drops.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and sentiment <0.2, reduce by 2–5% to avoid overbought trap.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.15 within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day to reflect delayed market reaction.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising — cap forecast at +3% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is consistently below 0.10, model should not forecast >70 unless strong macro catalysts are confirmed — avoid “sentiment-blind” spikes.
